steps.title: Launch the Experiential Learning Community
steps.summary: Launch the Experiential Learning Community as the prototype for King's wider Strategic Communities of Practice model. Mobilise growing interest across faculties in developing more experiential and internship-like learning within the curriculum by connecting interested colleagues from faculties and professional services. Hold an informal pre-launch event in July, establish a dedicated Teams space for the emerging community, and formally launch it through an Unconference on 14 September 2026. Use the Unconference to share existing practice, form new connections, surface ideas and potential collaborations, begin a King's Taxonomy of Experiential Learning, agree practical next steps and aspirations for the community's first year, and identify a small group of informal community leads or champions who can help sustain participation and mobilise early activity alongside Mark Peace and King's Academy. These will be voluntary, interim mobilisation roles without a central workload-release entitlement. They will not constitute appointment as a future funded convenor or confer an automatic advantage in a subsequent convenor selection process. Complete this prototype launch phase by the end of September 2026. The experience of forming the community, sustaining participation through Teams and translating the launch into collaborative activity will inform the common model used for subsequent communities.

outputs.owner: Mark Peace
outputs.summary: A cross-institutional network of faculty and professional-services colleagues brought together through the July pre-launch, wider engagement and the September Unconference.
acceptanceCriteria: The July informal pre-launch event has taken place and helped identify the founding network.

outputs.owner: Mark Peace

Participant-led discussions, examples and ideas are captured.
The purpose of the community and routes for continued involvement are made clear.
The event creates visible connections between colleagues with related interests and potential collaborations.

outputs.title: Experiential Learning SCoP Teams space
outputs.owner: Mark Peace

acceptanceCriteria: The Teams space is provisioned before the Unconference and founding participants are invited.

Clear administration and moderation arrangements are in place.
Launch materials, the synthesis map and agreed next steps are published in the space.

acceptanceCriteria: The principal forms of experiential and internship-like learning surfaced during the day are represented.
Existing examples, shared ideas and potential connections are captured.
Areas requiring further definition or development are identified.
The synthesis map is published through the Teams space.

acceptanceCriteria: At least three practical priorities or collaboration strands are identified.
Interested contributors are associated with each strand where possible.
A small and appropriately diverse group of informal leads or champions is identified.
The informal group understands its role in connecting participants, progressing early priorities and helping shape the community’s first year.
The roles are explicitly described as voluntary and interim, without a central workload-release entitlement.
Informal leadership is clearly distinguished from the later open process for funded convenor appointments.

steps.title: Agree the SCoP Operating Model
steps.summary: By December 2026, agree the standard operating model for Strategic Communities of Practice. Define how communities are established and led, how they are resourced, what their funding may be used for, how decisions are made, how they are governed and held to account, and the minimum expectations for activity, outputs and institutional impact. Alongside this, develop an institutional proposition for workload release, workload allocation or backfill for community convenors and colleagues leading funded projects. Faculties will need to take a view on how this can operate consistently and fairly within their own workload and resource arrangements. Use evidence and learning from the Experiential Learning prototype while developing the model, and secure enough clarity to support the first funded convenor and community-project calls.

outputs.title: Standard SCoP operating model
outputs.owner: Mark Peace
outputs.summary: A clear and reusable model defining how Strategic Communities of Practice are established, led, supported, operated, reviewed, renewed and, where necessary, closed.
acceptanceCriteria: The model defines the responsibilities of convenors, members, the central support function and the governing committee.
The model sets expectations for participation, communication, collaboration and decision-making.
The relationship between community activity and institutional education priorities is clear.
The model is approved through the agreed senior education governance route by December 2026.

outputs.title: SCoP resourcing and eligible-use framework

acceptanceCriteria: The indicative resource envelope and its principal components are defined.
Eligible and ineligible uses of funding are clear, including support for purposeful activity, collaboration, inquiry, dissemination and institutional change.
Budget ownership, authorisation, monitoring and reporting arrangements are documented.
The framework is sufficiently clear to inform the first convenor and community-project calls.

outputs.title: SCoP governance and accountability framework
outputs.owner: Mark Peace with senior education governance sponsor
outputs.summary: A defined route through which communities agree plans and priorities, report on activity and expenditure, demonstrate progress and impact, and receive challenge, support and decisions about continuation or change.
acceptanceCriteria: The Innovation Committee's remit, membership, delegated authority and reporting route are agreed.
The process through which communities agree and report their plans, priorities and expenditure is defined.
Annual review, renewal, escalation and closure arrangements are documented.
The relationship between the Innovation Committee and existing education governance is clear.

outputs.title: Minimum expectations for SCoP activity, output and impact
outputs.owner: Mark Peace with King's Academy

Communities are expected to create tangible outputs, recommendations, resources, collaborations or other appropriate products.
Communities are expected to demonstrate evidence of influence on education, policy, practice or institutional decision-making.
A proportionate annual account of activity, learning, expenditure, outputs and impact is required.

outputs.owner: Mark Peace with faculty education leadership
outputs.summary: A credible institutional proposition for workload release, workload allocation or backfill for SCoP convenors and colleagues leading funded community projects.
acceptanceCriteria: Eligibility, indicative scale and duration of support are defined.
The relationship between central funding, faculty contribution and local workload arrangements is set out.
Approval, recording and review arrangements are defined.
Faculty positions are sufficiently clear to make a credible and equitable offer in the first funded calls, with any wider unresolved workload-policy questions routed separately.

outputs.title: King's Academy ownership and support model
outputs.owner: King's Academy
outputs.summary: A phased model through which a named King's Academy Portfolio Lead takes increasing ownership from Mark Peace, supported by permanent portfolio administration and coordination as convenors and projects change.
acceptanceCriteria: A named King's Academy SCoP Portfolio Lead, or an agreed appointment route, is confirmed.
Responsibilities and decision rights are clear across the Portfolio Lead, Portfolio Coordinator, individual convenors, project leads and the Innovation Committee.
A phased transfer of portfolio ownership from Mark Peace to King's Academy is agreed.
Initial permanent administrative capacity of 0.2 FTE is confirmed, with scaling assumptions for the three- and six-community portfolio.
Initial Portfolio Lead capacity of 0.1 FTE is costed as a recurrent BAU liability, with future increases considered through the formal review steps.

steps.title: Recognise and mobilise the AI in Education and Inclusive Education communities
steps.summary: During September and October 2026, recognise and connect the informal communities of practice already developing around AI in Education and Inclusive Education. Build from the people, networks, activity and informal leadership already in place rather than replacing or rebranding what is working. Identify a small group of informal leads or champions in each area to work alongside Mark Peace and King's Academy, broaden participation, articulate emerging priorities and help mobilise early activity. These will be voluntary, interim mobilisation roles without a central workload-release entitlement. They will not constitute appointment as future funded convenors or confer an automatic advantage in subsequent convenor selection. By the end of October, connect both communities, together with the Experiential Learning Community launched through Step 1, to the emerging common SCoP operating model and the more sustained community-building work in Step 4.

outputs.owner: Mark Peace with King's Academy
outputs.summary: A proportionate, relationship-led picture of the people, networks, activity, communication routes and institutional connections already present in each area, providing a basis for mobilisation without imposing a new structure prematurely.
acceptanceCriteria: Existing networks, forums, communication spaces, regular activity and visible areas of interest are identified for both communities.
Colleagues already providing informal leadership, coordination or connective work are recognised.
Important gaps in faculty, disciplinary, professional-services or other relevant participation are identified.
The mobilisation approach builds from existing identities and activity rather than assuming that every network must be absorbed, renamed or replaced.

outputs.title: Informal mobilisation leadership identified
outputs.owner: Mark Peace with King's Academy
outputs.summary: A small group of informal leads or champions for AI in Education and for Inclusive Education, able to connect existing participants, broaden involvement, articulate priorities and help mobilise each community alongside the wider SCoP programme.
acceptanceCriteria: A small group of informal leads or champions is identified for each community rather than relying on a single individual where this can reasonably be avoided.
The groups reflect an appropriate breadth of existing activity and institutional participation.
The role is described as voluntary, interim and proportionate, without a central workload-release entitlement.
The role is clearly distinguished from later funded convenor appointments and does not confer an automatic advantage in an open selection process.
The informal leads understand the support available from Mark Peace, the King's Academy Portfolio Lead and the Portfolio Coordinator.

outputs.title: Initial mobilisation plans agreed
outputs.owner: Informal community leads with Mark Peace and King's Academy
outputs.summary: A light-touch mobilisation route for each community, connecting existing activity to wider participation and defining practical next steps before the sustained development phase.
acceptanceCriteria: Each community has a clear route through which interested colleagues can join or remain connected.
An appropriate existing or new communication space is identified, with proportionate administration arrangements.
One or more initial priorities, questions or activity strands are agreed for each community.
Immediate actions and informal owners are recorded without creating an unfunded programme of work that exceeds the voluntary nature of the roles.
The handoff into Step 4 is clear, including what should be developed, broadened or tested during the subsequent community-building phase.

outputs.title: Three communities connected within the emerging SCoP frame
outputs.owner: King's Academy Portfolio Lead with Mark Peace
outputs.summary: Experiential Learning, AI in Education and Inclusive Education each have identifiable informal mobilisation leadership and a clear relationship with the emerging common operating model, portfolio support and later funded-convenor process.
acceptanceCriteria: The Experiential Learning informal leads established through Step 1 are recognised alongside the equivalent groups for AI in Education and Inclusive Education.
All three communities have a named route into the King's Academy Portfolio Lead and Portfolio Coordinator.
The emerging operating model, current support arrangements and expectations for the mobilisation period are communicated consistently across the three communities.
The temporary status of informal leadership and the later open route to funded convenorship are clear.
All three communities are ready to enter the sustained community-building and operating-conventions work in Step 4 by the end of October 2026.

steps.title: Refine the operating model by piloting the first three communities
steps.summary: From November 2026 to June 2027, pilot the emerging Strategic Communities of Practice operating model through the Experiential Learning, AI in Education and Inclusive Education communities. Begin once the three communities have been mobilised through Step 3, supporting them to operate under their informal mobilisation leadership, sustain and broaden participation, deliver useful activity and pursue emerging priorities. Use the governance, accountability, budget-control and escalation arrangements sufficiently settled through the Step 2 design work, and bring the pilots fully within the approved framework as it is finalised, with clear decision rights and institutional oversight through King's Academy and the Innovation Committee. Use live operation to test whether the model is practical, proportionate and sufficiently supportive, refining processes, guidance and conventions without reopening the fundamental authority or accountability of the governance framework. Capture the evidence and continuity requirements needed to transfer leadership to funded convenors and integrate funded projects from September 2027. Informal leads remain voluntary and interim during this phase and do not assume the full accountability intended for later funded convenors.

outputs.title: Three community pilots operating
outputs.owner: Informal community leads with King's Academy
outputs.summary: Experiential Learning, AI in Education and Inclusive Education each operate as an active pilot community with an identifiable constituency, a clear participation route, functioning informal leadership and sustained communication across the pilot period.
acceptanceCriteria: Each community has a short pilot plan setting out its initial priorities, participation route, indicative activity and relationship to the common operating model.
Each community has an active communication space and a clear route through which interested colleagues can join or remain involved.
Participation extends beyond the informal leads and shows evidence of broadening across relevant faculties, disciplines, professional-services areas or other constituencies.
Informal leadership is shared where possible, remains explicitly voluntary and interim, and is supported rather than replaced by central portfolio capacity.
The three communities remain active throughout the November 2026-June 2027 pilot rather than relying on a single launch event or isolated meeting.

outputs.title: Community-led programmes of activity delivered
outputs.owner: Informal community leads with the King's Academy Portfolio Lead
outputs.summary: A proportionate programme in each community that responds to its own priorities while demonstrating the practical value of sustained exchange, collaboration and institutionally connected activity.
acceptanceCriteria: Each community delivers at least two purposeful activities during the pilot period rather than being limited to routine coordination meetings.

Activities may include practice exchange, collaborative inquiry, workshops, resource development, institutional propositions, student involvement, external engagement or connections between related initiatives.
Each community uses its operating allowance to support at least one event, guest speaker, specialist contributor, student group or external partner where this is relevant to its priorities.
Each community produces at least one tangible output, collaboration, recommendation or proposition through its pilot activity.
Activity, participation, expenditure and emerging outputs are recorded proportionately through the shared community and portfolio arrangements.

outputs.title: Governance and accountability demonstrated in practice
outputs.owner: King's Academy Portfolio Lead with the Innovation Committee
outputs.summary: The approved governance framework is used consistently across the three pilots, providing visible institutional authority, oversight and financial control while preserving appropriate community autonomy.
acceptanceCriteria: The Innovation Committee or agreed governing forum is operational and understands its delegated authority in time to exercise effective oversight of the pilots.
Decision rights are clear across informal community leads, the King's Academy Portfolio Lead, the Portfolio Coordinator, Mark Peace and the governing forum.
Each community has a clear route for advice, approval, escalation and influence on institutional education policy or practice.
Budget ownership, delegated approval, expenditure records and material commitments are managed consistently across all three communities.
Each community provides an approved pilot plan and budget, a light-touch midpoint update and an end-of-pilot account covering participation, activity, expenditure, outputs, risks and emerging impact.
Material decisions, exceptions and unresolved risks are recorded and routed through the agreed governance arrangements.
The governance arrangements are judged sufficiently robust to support funded convenors and community-aligned projects from September 2027.

outputs.title: Operating model refined through pilot evidence
outputs.owner: King's Academy Portfolio Lead with Mark Peace
outputs.summary: An evidence-led refinement of the common operating model that confirms the institutional controls that must remain consistent, improves practical processes and identifies where communities should retain flexibility.
acceptanceCriteria: The pilot synthesis distinguishes elements of governance, accountability, delegated authority, budget control, reporting, escalation and review that remain fixed across all communities.
Practical guidance is refined for participation, onboarding, communication, shared leadership, priority-setting, collaborative activity, evidence collection and routes into institutional influence.
Differences between the three communities are used to identify where standardisation would be unhelpful or disproportionate.
The actual demand placed on informal leads, the Portfolio Lead, the Portfolio Coordinator and temporary project-management capacity is assessed.
The adequacy and eligible use of the base community activity allowance are assessed against actual pilot activity and outcomes.

The Innovation Committee formally receives the pilot synthesis, approves refinements within its authority and escalates any material governance or resource changes through the agreed senior education route.

outputs.title: Transition packs for funded convenors and projects
outputs.owner: Informal community leads with the King's Academy Portfolio Coordinator
outputs.summary: A proportionate handover position for each community so that funded convenors and project teams can inherit and strengthen established relationships and activity rather than restarting the communities in September 2027.
acceptanceCriteria: Each transition pack records the community constituency, participation routes, active relationships, current priorities, work underway and commitments already made.
The expectations community members have of the funded convenor and the support required from the portfolio team are captured.
Outputs, propositions or collaborations requiring continuity into the funded cycle are identified.
Leadership-transition risks and sensitivities are recorded, including how informal leads will remain involved without being treated as pre-selected or displaced.
The packs are available in time to inform Step 5 appointment, mobilisation and handover arrangements.

newInvestment.item: Base community activity and engagement allowance

newInvestment.rationale: Establishes a minimum viable recurrent operating allowance of £4,000 per community per full academic year, with an initial £2,000 per community envelope for the November 2026-June 2027 pilot. It is separate from convenor workload release, permanent staffing and substantive funded projects, which are added through later steps.

enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The pilot may depend on excessive goodwill or turn informal leadership into an unfunded substitute for convenorship.

risks.title: Pilot language undermines confidence in institutional governance
risks.mitigation: Communicate that the governance and accountability framework has already been approved and that the pilot tests practical operation and proportionality, not whether governance is required. Keep decision rights, reporting, budget control and escalation visible throughout.

risks.title: Informal leads become de facto unfunded convenors
risks.mitigation: Keep the role shared, voluntary, interim and bounded; place administration and formal budget control with the portfolio team; and reserve substantive accountability and workload support for the funded appointments.

risks.title: A common operating model over-standardises different communities
risks.mitigation: Separate fixed institutional controls from flexible community practices and use evidence from all three pilots to identify where variation is necessary and productive.

risks.title: The recurrent activity allowance becomes an untested entitlement
risks.mitigation: Treat £4,000 per community as a planning assumption, review its adequacy and use through the pilot, and base later portfolio scaling on evidence while preserving the initial £12,000 annual BAU liability unless formally revised.

risks.title: Activity is visible but produces weak learning or continuity
risks.mitigation: Use agreed pilot plans, midpoint updates, proportionate evidence and transition packs so that activity informs operating-model refinement and the September 2027 funded handover.

steps.title: Commission the first funded community and project cycle
steps.summary: From January to March 2027, move the Experiential Learning, AI in Education and Inclusive Education communities from an initial phase sustained largely through informal coalescing, professional goodwill and enthusiasm towards a more durable funded model for the 2027-28 academic year. Run an open call to identify and support a very small number of funded convenors who can provide consistent leadership across the three communities, normally one or two convenors per community appointed for two academic years. Alongside this, invite proposals for approximately five practice-based projects that advance the priorities and development of the communities, creating useful activity, collaboration, outputs and institutional learning rather than funding disconnected projects or a general research-grant scheme. Agree the successful convenors and project portfolio by the end of March, together with written faculty or organisational commitments in principle, the protected-capacity model, reserved funding authority, governance and reporting expectations, and the April-August preparation route required for activity to begin in September 2027. Relevant learning from the Step 4 pilots should inform the process and handover as it becomes available, but completion of the pilots is not a prerequisite for commissioning the funded cycle. The purpose is not to replace the energy, relationships and distributed participation through which the communities have formed, but to provide enough protected leadership and practical project support for that activity to become sustainable, purposeful and institutionally connected.

outputs.title: Open convenor and practice-based project calls delivered
outputs.owner: King's Academy SCoP Portfolio Lead and Portfolio Coordinator
outputs.summary: Coordinated but distinct open calls through which funded convenors and practice-based projects are invited, supported and assessed as parts of one coherent community portfolio.
acceptanceCriteria: The convenor call defines the role, two-academic-year term, expected contribution, accountability, indicative protected capacity and relationship with King's Academy and the Innovation Committee.
The call permits one or two convenors per community, with a single 0.1 FTE community-level allocation shared where co-convenors are appointed.
The project call seeks approximately five practice-based projects across the portfolio and defines eligibility, purpose, delivery period, expected outputs, reporting and eligible direct costs.

Each project is offered an indicative 0.1 FTE release, workload allocation or backfill envelope for one academic year, divisible across a small project team, together with up to £1,000 for direct delivery costs.

The 0.1 FTE project assumption is presented as a costable planning proxy broadly comparable to leading a 15-credit unit, subject to validation through the relevant faculty or organisational workload model.
Academic and professional-services staff, collaborative staff teams and teams involving students or external partners may apply, provided a named King's staff member holds responsibility.
Assessment criteria, decision rights, timetable, applicant guidance and conflict-of-interest arrangements are published before applications open.
Informal mobilisation leads are eligible to apply through the open process but receive no automatic status or selection advantage.

outputs.title: Funded convenors commissioned for the first three communities
outputs.owner: Innovation Committee on the recommendation of the convenor selection panel
outputs.summary: One or two funded convenors commissioned for each of the three communities, with protected capacity and credible institutional support for a September 2027 start.
acceptanceCriteria: Each of the Experiential Learning, AI in Education and Inclusive Education communities has one or two approved funded convenors.
Convenors are appointed for the 2027-28 and 2028-29 academic years, subject to satisfactory annual review rather than annual reapplication.
Each community has an agreed protected-capacity envelope equivalent to 0.1 FTE, or approximately half a day per week, shared where two convenors are appointed.
Selection considers community-building capability, institutional reach, strategic judgement, inclusive leadership and the ability to translate community activity into useful outputs and influence.
The relevant faculty or organisational area provides written confirmation in principle of how release, workload allocation or backfill will be enabled from September 2027.
The role, term, responsibilities, accountability and decision rights are clear across convenors, the SCoP Portfolio Lead, the Portfolio Coordinator and the Innovation Committee.
Any co-convening arrangement records how the shared protected capacity and leadership responsibilities will be divided.
Unsuccessful applicants receive a clear outcome and an appropriate feedback route.

outputs.title: First practice-based project portfolio commissioned
outputs.owner: Innovation Committee on the recommendation of the project selection panel
outputs.summary: Approximately five practice-based projects commissioned as a coherent portfolio that advances one or more of the three communities and creates useful educational practice, collaboration and institutional learning.
acceptanceCriteria: Approximately five projects are selected across the portfolio, with no automatic or equal allocation by community.
Each project is clearly connected to one or more communities and to an identified education priority, challenge or opportunity.
Each project has a named King's lead, defined purpose, intended beneficiaries, outputs, delivery period, evidence approach and preparation route.
Each project has an approved 0.1 FTE release, workload allocation or backfill envelope for one academic year and up to £1,000 for direct delivery costs, to become operational through Step 7.
Projects are additional to ordinary business and do not fund activity that should already be delivered through established roles or budgets.
The final portfolio considers quality, strategic relevance, feasibility, diversity of approach, duplication and opportunities for cross-community collaboration.

Preferred convenors may advise on community fit and portfolio coherence, but formal decisions remain with an independent panel or the Innovation Committee and all conflicts of interest are declared and managed.
The option not to allocate all funding, to retain a reserve list or to run a targeted second-stage process is preserved where proposal quality is insufficient.

outputs.title: Institutional commitments and commissioning confirmations secured
outputs.owner: King's Academy SCoP Portfolio Lead with faculties, Finance and organisational sponsors
outputs.summary: The selected portfolio moves beyond a preferred list: the institutional, faculty and funding commitments required for a credible September start are agreed by the end of March.
acceptanceCriteria: Written faculty or organisational commitment in principle is secured for every selected convenor and project requiring release, workload allocation or backfill.

Funding authority is confirmed and reserved for the Step 7 operating requirement: 0.3 FTE of convenor capacity across three communities, approximately 0.5 FTE across five annual projects and up to £5,000 of direct project expenditure.
The funding source, budget holder, authorisation route and financial-control expectations are identified.
Conditional offers or commissioning confirmations are issued to successful convenors and project leads by the end of March 2027.
Any outstanding HR, workload, financial or administrative conditions have named owners and deadlines during April-August.
No selected convenor or project remains dependent on an unspecified later decision about whether the agreed capacity or direct-cost funding will exist.
The resource commitment is handed forward to Step 7, where the funded capacity and expenditure become operational; it is not duplicated as new delivery investment in Step 5.

outputs.title: April-August preparation and community handover route agreed
outputs.owner: King's Academy SCoP Portfolio Coordinator
outputs.summary: A clear route through which successful convenors, project leads, faculties and King's Academy complete the practical preparation required for the funded cycle to begin in September 2027.
acceptanceCriteria: Each convenor and project lead has a proportionate onboarding and preparation timetable for April-August.
Named owners are assigned for formal workload processing, budget setup, commissioning documentation, induction, community planning and project readiness.
The transition from informal mobilisation leadership to funded convening is planned sensitively and does not displace existing community relationships or participation.
Relevant learning, continuity material and transition packs from Step 4 can be incorporated as they become available without reopening the core commissioning decisions.
Each community will have an agreed September-June activity plan and each project an agreed delivery plan before the funded cycle begins.
A readiness checkpoint is scheduled before September 2027, with a clear route for resolving outstanding conditions or adjusting scope.

risks.title: Informal mobilisation leads are perceived as pre-selected

risks.mitigation: Require written commitment in principle and a named local owner before final commissioning, with explicit summer deadlines for completing workload or backfill arrangements.

risks.title: Convenor and project selections do not form a coherent portfolio
risks.mitigation: Select preferred convenors before final project decisions, invite proportionate advice on community fit, and retain independent portfolio-level decision-making through the Innovation Committee.

risks.title: The first calls produce weak or uneven applications
risks.mitigation: Provide briefings and proposal-development support, preserve the option not to allocate all funding, use a reserve list and run a targeted second-stage process where necessary.

risks.mitigation: Do not describe the cycle as commissioned until funding authority, written local commitment, named implementation owners and deadlines are in place.

risks.title: Funded leadership displaces the goodwill and distributed participation that formed the communities
risks.mitigation: Define convening as enabling and connecting rather than owning the community, use Step 4 continuity material and plan a sensitive handover from informal mobilisation leadership.

risks.title: Project funding becomes a general research-grant scheme or substitutes for ordinary business
risks.mitigation: Require a clear practice-based contribution to one or more communities, additionality to existing responsibilities and tangible educational practice, collaboration or institutional learning.

assumptions.title: Community-level convenor capacity

assumptions.title: Project-level protected capacity

assumptions.title: Annual project commissioning and two-year convenor terms
assumptions.summary: Practice-based projects are commissioned for one academic-year cycle, while convenors are appointed for two academic years subject to satisfactory annual review.

assumptions.title: Delivery investment begins in Step 7
assumptions.summary: Step 5 approves and reserves the future resource commitment. Convenor capacity, project release or backfill and direct project expenditure become operational from September 2027 and are recorded as delivery resource in Step 7 rather than duplicated here.

steps.title: Review the first mobilisation, agree the 2028-29 community portfolio and launch the next calls
steps.summary: From July to August 2027, review the initial mobilisation and pilot operation of the Experiential Learning, AI in Education and Inclusive Education communities together with the first process for commissioning funded convenors and practice-based projects. Use this evidence to refine the operating, governance, commissioning and central-support arrangements before the portfolio expands, while recognising that the first funded operating cycle will not begin until September 2027 and therefore cannot yet be evaluated for delivery impact. Establish a proportionate success framework for reach and impact that can be used from the first funded cycle, drawing on the initial pilots to establish baselines where possible and agreeing portfolio expectations, evidence responsibilities and reporting arrangements. In parallel, look forward to the academic year beginning in September 2028. Review the Education Delivery Framework with the Vice President (Education and Student Success) and the Vice Deans Education to identify and agree the three additional education priorities around which the next Strategic Communities of Practice should be established. Confirm the proposed six-community portfolio for 2028-29, the resource and central-support implications of expansion, and any refinements required to the convenor and practice-based project model. Launch the calls that will be commissioned between January and March 2028, allowing detailed preparation and community formation between April and August ahead of operation from September 2028. The call should seek funded convenors for the three additional communities and the next annual portfolio of approximately five practice-based projects across the planned six-community model. Convenors appointed to the original three communities through Step 5 will normally remain in post for the second year of their two-academic-year term.

outputs.title: Initial mobilisation and first commissioning review completed
outputs.owner: King's Academy SCoP Portfolio Lead with Mark Peace and the Innovation Committee
outputs.summary: A focused review of the first three community pilots and the first convenor and practice-based project commissioning process, identifying what should be retained, refined or resolved before expansion.
acceptanceCriteria: The review distinguishes evidence from the initial mobilisation and pilots from evidence about the funded operating cycle, which has not yet begun.
The review considers sustained participation, distributed contribution, informal leadership, community activity, governance, budget control, reporting and the transition towards funded convening.

The first commissioning process is reviewed for application quality and diversity, clarity of the offer, faculty or organisational commitment, workload and backfill practicality, panel operation, conflicts of interest, decision timing and applicant experience.
The suitability of the 0.1 FTE convenor and project planning assumptions and the up-to-£1,000 direct project-cost offer is considered without duplicating the Step 7 delivery investment.
Actionable refinements are agreed with named owners and are incorporated into the 2028-29 call and operating arrangements.
The review records matters that cannot yet be judged and identifies the evidence to be gathered through the first funded cycle.

outputs.title: Reach and impact success framework established
outputs.owner: King's Academy SCoP Portfolio Lead with the Innovation Committee
outputs.summary: A common but proportionate framework through which the portfolio, individual communities and funded projects can demonstrate who they are engaging, the depth and breadth of participation, the practice they develop and spread, and their influence on students and institutional education priorities.
acceptanceCriteria: A small common core of deliverable-level measures is agreed for active reach and institutional breadth, depth of participation and distributed leadership, practice development and spread, institutional influence, and student-facing impact.
Definitions distinguish nominal reach, such as mailing-list membership or one-off attendance, from active, repeat and contributory participation.
Evidence from the first three pilots is used to establish initial baselines where reliable evidence exists, and gaps in the baseline are explicitly recorded.
Evidence-informed targets or qualitative success thresholds are agreed for the 2027-28 funded cycle and the planned six-community portfolio beginning in September 2028.
Every community uses the common core measures and may add a small number of theme-specific measures that reflect its intended contribution.
Every funded project states its intended reach, practical change and proportionate evidence of impact before delivery begins.
Responsibilities and data sources are clear across convenors, project leads, the Portfolio Coordinator, the Portfolio Lead and the Innovation Committee.
Evidence requirements remain proportionate, avoid vanity metrics and do not expect every community to demonstrate direct institution-wide or student-outcome effects within a single year.
The annual review process explains how reach and impact evidence will inform support, continuation, expansion, commissioning and institutional decision-making.

outputs.title: Three additional strategic community themes agreed
outputs.owner: Vice President (Education and Student Success) with the Vice Deans Education
outputs.summary: Three additional education priorities agreed as the basis for new Strategic Communities of Practice beginning in September 2028, following review of the Education Delivery Framework.
acceptanceCriteria: The Education Delivery Framework is reviewed for the cross-cutting priorities that require active institutional development during 2028-29 and beyond.
The Vice President (Education and Student Success) and the Vice Deans Education consider and agree the proposed three additional themes.
The rationale for each theme, its intended institutional contribution and its relationship to the Education Delivery Framework are recorded.
Each theme has a sufficiently clear and distinctive purpose to justify a Strategic Community of Practice rather than another form of project, committee or network.
Potential overlap with existing groups, programmes, governance structures and professional-service responsibilities is considered and resolved or explicitly managed.
A preliminary viability assessment identifies likely cross-faculty and professional-service interest and the route through which a founding community can be formed before September 2028.
The choice of themes is a strategic education-portfolio decision rather than an open popularity contest, while evidence of existing energy and expertise informs viability.

outputs.title: Six-community expansion proposition approved
outputs.owner: Vice President (Education and Student Success) and the Innovation Committee with King's Academy
outputs.summary: An approved proposition for the six-community model beginning in September 2028, including refined operating assumptions, annual project commissioning and the central support required to prepare and sustain the larger portfolio.
acceptanceCriteria: The six-community portfolio and intended September 2028 start are confirmed, or any justified adjustment to scale or pace is recorded.
The model continues to allow one or two convenors per community, with a shared 0.1 FTE community allocation and two-academic-year appointments unless the review supports a documented refinement.

The annual practice-based project model remains a portfolio of approximately five projects across all six communities, each normally supported by a 0.1 FTE protected-capacity allocation and up to £1,000 direct costs, unless the review supports a documented refinement.
The original three convenors are expected to remain in post for the second year of their Step 5 appointment and are not required to reapply routinely.

The additional central capacity required to prepare and operate the expanded portfolio is confirmed, including the planning assumption that the Portfolio Lead increases from 0.1 to 0.2 FTE and the Portfolio Coordinator from 0.2 to 0.4 FTE.
The resource source, timing, budget-holding route and recurrent implications of the additional central capacity are agreed before the expansion calls create commitments.
The proposition explains how the three additional communities will form founding networks and develop priorities between commissioning and the September 2028 start.

outputs.title: 2028-29 convenor and practice-based project calls launched
outputs.owner: King's Academy SCoP Portfolio Lead and Portfolio Coordinator
outputs.summary: Calls launched for convenors of the three additional communities and for the next annual practice-based project portfolio across the planned six-community model, for commissioning through Step 8 between January and March 2028.
acceptanceCriteria: The convenor call covers the three additional communities and appointments beginning in September 2028 for two academic years.
The call only includes the original three communities where an exceptional vacancy or documented leadership change requires action.
The project call seeks approximately five practice-based projects across the six-community portfolio for delivery during 2028-29, without guaranteeing equal allocation by community.
The calls incorporate agreed learning from the Step 4 pilots, Step 5 commissioning process and Step 6 review.
The reach and impact framework is embedded proportionately in the role, application, assessment and reporting expectations for convenors and projects.
Eligibility, resource offers, assessment criteria, faculty or organisational commitments, conflict controls, timetable and decision rights are clear.
Applicants and faculties have sufficient time to develop credible proposals before the January-March 2028 commissioning window.
The calls explain the April-August 2028 preparation and community-formation period and the September 2028 operating start.

decisions.summary: Agree what the pilot and first commissioning evidence supports changing before expansion, what should be retained and what remains untested until the funded operating cycle has run.

decisions.title: Approve the reach and impact success framework
decisions.summary: Agree the common measure set, definitions, baselines, initial targets or qualitative thresholds, evidence responsibilities and reporting cadence for the first funded and future six-community cycles.

decisions.summary: Following review of the Education Delivery Framework, the Vice President (Education and Student Success) and Vice Deans Education approve the three additional strategic education priorities for communities beginning in September 2028.

decisions.summary: Confirm the intended six-community portfolio, any refinement to the convenor and project model, and the additional recurrent Portfolio Lead and Portfolio Coordinator capacity required to prepare and sustain expansion.

risks.title: The review overclaims evidence from the first mobilisation
risks.mitigation: Separate pilot and commissioning evidence from the performance of the funded cycle, explicitly record what cannot yet be judged and carry those questions into Step 7 evidence collection.

risks.title: Success measures reward visibility rather than meaningful reach or impact
risks.mitigation: Distinguish mailing-list and one-off attendance from active, repeat and contributory participation, combine quantitative evidence with proportionate qualitative judgement and review measures that create perverse incentives.

risks.title: Student-facing or institutional impact is claimed without credible attribution
risks.mitigation: Use contribution language, evidence chains and bounded case studies; do not require direct causal student-outcome claims where the evidence cannot support them.

risks.title: Evidence requirements become too burdensome
risks.mitigation: Use a small common core, reuse normal community and project records, permit theme-specific evidence and make the Portfolio Coordinator responsible for maintaining the portfolio evidence structure.

risks.title: The next themes are strategically attractive but cannot form viable communities
risks.mitigation: Combine senior strategic selection through the Education Delivery Framework with a preliminary viability assessment of expertise, cross-institutional interest, overlap and a route to founding participation.

risks.title: Expansion outpaces central support capacity
risks.mitigation: Make the recurrent support decision before the calls create commitments and adjust the scale, timetable or support model if the additional capacity cannot be secured.

risks.title: The original three convenors are inadvertently destabilised by the next call
risks.mitigation: State clearly that they remain in the second year of their appointments and include those communities only where an exceptional vacancy or documented change requires action.

risks.title: Calls are launched too late or without enough clarity for credible proposals
risks.mitigation: Complete theme, resource, measure and call decisions within the July-August window and publish a clear timetable leading to Step 8 commissioning between January and March 2028.

assumptions.title: The first funded cycle has not yet run

assumptions.title: Original convenors remain in post
assumptions.summary: Convenors appointed through Step 5 normally serve through 2027-28 and 2028-29 and therefore do not routinely reapply in the calls launched through this step.

assumptions.title: Projects continue as an annual portfolio
assumptions.summary: Approximately five practice-based projects are commissioned annually across the whole planned six-community portfolio rather than allocated automatically or equally to individual communities.

assumptions.title: Common core with theme-specific evidence
assumptions.summary: All communities and projects use a small common reach and impact framework, while additional evidence can reflect the distinct contribution and maturity of each theme.

assumptions.title: Baselines precede numerical targets
assumptions.summary: Step 6 uses the initial pilots to establish reliable baselines where possible and then agrees evidence-informed numerical targets or qualitative success thresholds rather than inventing false precision in advance.

steps.title: Operate the first funded three-community cycle
steps.summary: From September 2027 to June 2028, operate the first fully funded Strategic Communities of Practice cycle across Experiential Learning, AI in Education and Inclusive Education. Bring the funded convenors appointed through Step 5 into their roles, activate the agreed release, workload-allocation or backfill arrangements, and deliver a visible programme of community activity aligned to the priorities of each community. Maintain the distributed participation and professional energy through which the communities originally formed, while using protected convenor capacity to provide continuity, connection, purposeful leadership and institutional influence. Deliver approximately five practice-based projects across the portfolio. Each project should use its protected capacity and direct-cost allowance to develop, test or spread useful educational practice, create collaboration and generate institutional learning rather than operating as a disconnected research project. Apply the common reach and impact framework established through Step 6, gathering proportionate evidence of active reach, distributed leadership, practice development and spread, institutional influence and student-facing educational impact. Use termly review points to identify where communities or projects need support, adaptation or escalation, and complete a year-end portfolio account by June 2028 to inform the formal operating-cycle review in Step 9.

outputs.title: Funded community leadership and annual plans operational
outputs.owner: King's Academy SCoP Portfolio Lead with the funded convenors
outputs.summary: The first funded convenors are active in role, their protected capacity is operating, and each of the three communities has an agreed September-June plan connected to its strategic education purpose.
acceptanceCriteria: The Experiential Learning, AI in Education and Inclusive Education communities each have one or two funded convenors active in role for the first year of their two-academic-year appointments.
The shared 0.1 FTE community-level protected-capacity arrangement is activated for each community and any co-convenor split is implemented as commissioned.

Each community has an approved September-June plan covering priorities, participation, activity, collaboration, intended outputs, institutional contribution, reach and impact evidence, budget and principal risks.
Responsibilities and decision rights are clear across convenors, community contributors, the Portfolio Lead, the Portfolio Coordinator and the Innovation Committee.
Convenors use their protected role to enable and connect distributed participation rather than becoming the sole deliverers of all community activity.
The handover from informal mobilisation leadership preserves useful relationships, continuity and routes for existing contributors to remain involved.

outputs.title: Three funded community programmes delivered
outputs.owner: Funded community convenors
outputs.summary: A visible and purposeful programme of activity delivered by each community, supporting exchange, collaboration, development of practice and contribution to institutional education priorities.
acceptanceCriteria: Each community delivers a visible programme of activity across the academic year rather than relying on a single launch or event.
Activity creates regular opportunities for colleagues to exchange, develop, test or spread educational practice and to form useful collaborations.
Participation and contribution extend beyond the funded convenor or convenors and include appropriate cross-faculty and professional-services representation.
Each community produces or progresses tangible outputs, recommendations, resources, collaborations or other products appropriate to its theme.
Community insight is connected to relevant faculty and institutional education discussions, including the Education Delivery Framework where appropriate.
The continuing £4,000 annual base activity allowance per community is used in accordance with the Step 2 eligible-use framework and is reported without being counted again as new Step 7 investment.

outputs.title: First funded practice-based project portfolio delivered
outputs.owner: Funded project leads with the relevant community convenors
outputs.summary: Approximately five funded projects delivered across the three-community portfolio, each developing, testing or spreading useful educational practice and contributing to one or more communities.
acceptanceCriteria: Approximately five commissioned projects begin with named leads, delivery teams, confirmed community connections, agreed outputs, timetable, budget and evidence approach.
The 0.1 FTE project-level release, workload-allocation or backfill arrangement is activated for each project and may be divided across a small team within the commissioned envelope.
Each project may use up to £1,000 of direct delivery expenditure for eligible costs and maintains proportionate financial records.
Projects remain connected to one or more communities through shared activity, challenge, dissemination, collaboration or contribution to community priorities.
Each project delivers the agreed practical output or learning and records evidence of use, adoption, adaptation, further development or credible potential for spread.
Projects normally complete by June 2028; any extension is exceptional, time-limited, approved through the agreed governance route and does not obscure the performance of the annual portfolio.
Material underspend, non-delivery or change of scope is identified early and addressed through support, re-scoping, recovery, reallocation or closure.

outputs.title: Reach, impact and institutional influence evidenced
outputs.owner: King's Academy SCoP Portfolio Coordinator and Portfolio Lead with convenors and project leads
outputs.summary: The common reach and impact framework established in Step 6 is applied proportionately across the live communities and projects, generating usable evidence rather than vanity metrics or unsupported claims.
acceptanceCriteria: Termly evidence is gathered against the five common measures: active reach and institutional breadth; depth of participation and distributed leadership; practice development and spread; institutional influence; and student-facing educational impact.
Mailing-list membership and one-off attendance are distinguished from active, repeat and contributory participation.
Participation gaps, institutional concentrations and unequal patterns of contribution are made visible and prompt proportionate support or adaptation.
Evidence distinguishes production of outputs from actual use, adoption, adaptation or spread.
Community recommendations and insight entering faculty or institutional decision routes are recorded together with what happened as a result.
Student-facing impact is evidenced through bounded and proportionate evidence chains or case studies without claiming causality that the evidence cannot support.
Evidence collection remains light-touch enough to support learning and accountability without crowding out community or project delivery.

outputs.title: First funded-cycle portfolio account completed
outputs.owner: King's Academy SCoP Portfolio Lead with the Innovation Committee
outputs.summary: A concise but substantive account of the first funded cycle, providing the evidence handoff required for the formal review in Step 9.
acceptanceCriteria: The account covers each community and the overall portfolio, including activity, active participation, distributed leadership, outputs, project delivery and expenditure.
The account synthesises evidence of practice development and spread, institutional influence and student-facing contribution, including limitations and evidence gaps.
Material variation between communities or projects, unresolved risks, support needs, recovery actions and governance decisions are recorded transparently.
The status of every commissioned project is clear, including completion, approved extension, re-scope, closure, underspend or outstanding evidence.
The account identifies learning and questions requiring formal consideration through Step 9 without pre-empting that review.
The Innovation Committee receives and accepts the portfolio account by the end of June 2028.

existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: Administration, evidence and financial control may fall onto convenors or substantive leaders and weaken delivery or institutional memory.

existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The funded cycle may operate without consistent accountability, challenge, escalation or institutional decision-making.

existingCapacity.owner: Faculty education leadership, faculty operations, Finance, HR and relevant professional services

existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: Commissioned capacity may not translate into usable time and projects or communities may be blocked by local operational barriers.

decisions.title: Approve the three community and project delivery plans
decisions.summary: Confirm that the September-June plans, budgets, reach and impact intentions, responsibilities and risks remain consistent with the commissioned portfolio before substantive delivery begins.

decisions.title: Decide material changes, recovery or reallocation
decisions.summary: Use termly review points to approve significant changes of scope, recovery actions, project closure, use of reserve capacity or reallocation of uncommitted direct expenditure.

decisions.title: Decide exceptional project extensions
decisions.summary: Approve only time-limited and justified extensions beyond June 2028, with clear ownership, residual budget, evidence and an explanation of how the project will remain visible in the annual portfolio account.

decisions.title: Accept the first funded-cycle portfolio account
decisions.summary: Confirm that the year-end account provides a sufficiently complete and balanced evidence handoff for the formal Step 9 review.

risks.title: Approved protected capacity is not usable in practice
risks.mitigation: Track actual release or workload implementation from the start, require named local owners and escalate promptly where commissioned capacity is being absorbed by unchanged duties.

risks.title: Convenors become sole organisers rather than enablers of distributed leadership
risks.mitigation: Use annual plans and termly review to test the breadth of contribution, create explicit routes for members to lead activity and assess depth of participation separately from convenor delivery.

risks.title: Funded projects detach from their communities
risks.mitigation: Require ongoing community connection, include project activity in community programmes and review contribution to shared priorities rather than assessing projects only as standalone outputs.

risks.title: Reach is inflated by nominal membership and one-off attendance
risks.mitigation: Apply the Step 6 definitions consistently and report mailing lists and one-off attendance separately from active, repeat and contributory participation.

risks.title: Evidence collection becomes performative or burdensome
risks.mitigation: Use a small common core, reuse routine records, gather short bounded case studies and remove evidence requests that do not support learning, accountability or a real decision.

risks.title: Student-facing impact is overclaimed
risks.mitigation: Use proportionate contribution evidence, state limitations and avoid asserting direct causation or movement in common outcomes where the timeframe and evidence cannot support it.

risks.title: Performance varies sharply across communities or projects
risks.mitigation: Use termly review to identify variation early, provide tailored support and challenge, agree recovery or re-scope, and preserve transparent evidence rather than smoothing out differences at portfolio level.

risks.title: Expansion activity distracts central support from the live cycle
risks.mitigation: Protect the Step 6 central-capacity increase, plan commissioning activity explicitly and monitor whether support to operating communities or evidence quality is declining as the next portfolio is prepared.

assumptions.title: Convenor capacity is allocated per community
assumptions.summary: Each community has a total 0.1 FTE protected-capacity envelope, shared rather than duplicated where two convenors are appointed.

assumptions.title: Project capacity is allocated per project
assumptions.summary: Each commissioned project has an indicative 0.1 FTE protected-capacity envelope that may be divided across a small team, plus up to £1,000 of eligible direct delivery expenditure.

assumptions.title: Projects normally complete within the annual cycle
assumptions.summary: The first practice-based project portfolio normally completes by June 2028; extensions are exceptional and do not silently roll into the next annual commissioning cycle.

assumptions.title: Step 6 success definitions are operational before evidence is due
assumptions.summary: The reach and impact baselines, targets or qualitative thresholds, definitions, templates and ownership arrangements established through Step 6 are available early enough to shape delivery and termly review.

assumptions.title: Previously established recurrent capacity is not counted twice
assumptions.summary: The base community activity allowance and central Portfolio Lead and Coordinator capacity established through Steps 2, 4 and 6 remain visible as continuing capacity but are not duplicated as new Step 7 investment.

steps.title: Commission the expanded six-community portfolio
steps.summary: From January to March 2028, commission the expanded six-community operating cycle for September 2028. Assess the convenor and community-project calls launched through Step 6, agree renewed and new convenors and the funded project portfolio, and establish the faculty, workload, budget, governance, reporting and delivery arrangements required for all six communities to operate from September. Agree the preparation route through which the three additional communities will build their founding memberships and priorities and through which all successful convenors and project teams will be ready during April-August.

outputs.title: Six-community convenor and project portfolio commissioned
outputs.summary: Renewed and new convenors and community-aligned projects approved for the expanded operating cycle beginning in September 2028.

outputs.title: September 2028 operating arrangements agreed
outputs.summary: Workload, budgets, governance, reporting, onboarding and community-development arrangements agreed so that all six communities can prepare for the September start.

steps.title: Review the first funded operating cycle, refine the model and launch the 2029-30 calls
steps.summary: During July and August 2028, review and report on the completed September-June operating cycle. Assess participation, activity, impact, governance, convenorship, faculty release and backfill, funding, project mechanisms and institutional influence; refine the model for the expanded portfolio; and launch the 2029-30 convenor and community-project calls by the end of August. As part of the review, assess the workload required for the expanded six-community portfolio and decide whether to release the final planned increments in permanent King's Academy leadership and administration.

outputs.title: First funded-cycle impact and operating-model review
outputs.summary: An assessment of the first funded cycle with agreed refinements to governance, resourcing and operating arrangements for the expanded portfolio.

outputs.title: Open 2029-30 convenor and project calls
outputs.summary: Calls launched by the end of August for the next annual portfolio of convenors and community-aligned projects.

outputs.title: Support capacity agreed for the six-community portfolio
outputs.owner: King's Academy with Mark Peace
outputs.summary: An evidence-based decision on whether to increase permanent portfolio leadership and coordination capacity for the expanded six-community portfolio.
acceptanceCriteria: The actual workload from the first funded three-community cycle is reviewed.
The need for the planned increase to 0.3 FTE Portfolio Lead and 0.6 FTE Portfolio Coordinator capacity is confirmed, amended or declined.
Any approved incremental recurrent funding is in place for September 2028.

newInvestment.item: Additional King's Academy SCoP Portfolio Lead capacity for the six-community portfolio
newInvestment.rationale: Adds a further 0.1 FTE of recurrent Portfolio Lead capacity, taking the role from 0.2 to 0.3 FTE if the funded-cycle review confirms that this is required for the six-community portfolio.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: Strategic oversight, convenor support and cross-community learning may become too thin as the portfolio doubles in size.

newInvestment.item: Additional King's Academy SCoP Portfolio Coordinator capacity for the six-community portfolio
newInvestment.rationale: Adds a further 0.2 FTE of recurrent portfolio coordination, taking the role from 0.4 to 0.6 FTE if the review confirms that this is required to administer the six-community portfolio.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: The expanded annual cycle, committee workload, records, reporting and convenor handovers may not be administered reliably.

steps.title: Operate the six-community portfolio
steps.summary: Operate all six strategic communities through the September 2028-June 2029 academic-year cycle, supporting their funded convenors, programmes, projects, institutional influence and cross-community learning while gathering consistent evidence of participation, outcomes and resource requirements.

outputs.title: Full six-community operating cycle
outputs.summary: Six communities complete a coherent September-June cycle, including the contribution of their funded projects.

steps.title: Commission the 2029-30 portfolio and prepare institutional handover
steps.summary: From January to March 2029, commission the convenors and community-aligned projects for the operating cycle beginning in September 2029. Assess the calls launched through Step 9, agree the successful portfolio, and establish the workload, budget, governance, reporting, delivery and preparation arrangements required for the September start. In parallel, capture the operational, budget-holding, reporting and accountability requirements that must be incorporated into the permanent institutional handover, while allowing detailed onboarding and local preparation to continue during April-August.

outputs.title: 2029-30 portfolio commissioned
outputs.summary: Convenors and projects approved, with the institutional and local arrangements required for the September 2029 operating cycle agreed.

outputs.title: Institutional handover requirements prepared
outputs.summary: The practical operational, governance, budget-holding, reporting and resource requirements for transfer into the permanent model are documented.

steps.title: Review the six-community cycle and confirm the permanent model
steps.summary: During July and August 2029, review and report on the completed six-community operating cycle. Assess impact and sustainability, determine which communities should continue or evolve, and develop and approve the permanent institutional owner, governance arrangements, budget holding, recurrent resource settlement and annual planning cycle by the end of August. Use evidence from the operating cycles and the practical handover requirements captured through Step 11 to confirm or adjust the cumulative recurrent King's Academy portfolio leadership and administration settlement, without counting investment already introduced through earlier steps a second time.

outputs.title: Six-community impact and sustainability review
outputs.summary: A completed assessment of the expanded portfolio and its contribution after a full operating cycle.

outputs.title: Approved permanent institutional model
outputs.summary: Permanent ownership, governance, budget holding, recurrent resources and the annual commissioning and operating rhythm developed and approved by the end of August 2029.

outputs.title: Confirmed permanent SCoP support settlement
outputs.owner: King's Academy with the agreed governance route
outputs.summary: The final recurrent leadership and administrative capacity for the permanent SCoP portfolio, confirmed or amended using evidence from mobilisation and funded operating cycles.
acceptanceCriteria: The final Portfolio Lead and Portfolio Coordinator workload assumptions are agreed from evidence of actual demand.
Grades or backfill routes, recurrent costs, institutional owner and budget holder are confirmed.
The settlement explicitly recognises the recurrent liabilities introduced in Steps 2, 6 and 9 and does not count them again as new investment.

steps.title: Transition to business as usual
steps.summary: From September 2029, complete the transfer to the permanent institutional owner so that Strategic Communities of Practice continue through the established rhythm of September-June operation, July-August review, reporting and call launch, January-March commissioning, and April-August preparation for the following September start.

outputs.title: Business-as-usual transition complete
outputs.summary: Strategic Communities of Practice operate through permanent ownership, governance, recurrent resources and an established annual planning cycle from September 2029.
